question.problem: Expressed as a mixed number in its lowest terms, $3\,\frac{3}{5}\times 2\,\frac{1}{3}=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we write $3\,\frac{3}{5}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
3\,\frac{3}{5}=\frac{(3\times 5)+3}{5}=\frac{18}{5}
$$

We also write $2\,\frac{1}{3}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
2\,\frac{1}{3}=\frac{(2\times 3)+1}{3}=\frac{7}{3}
$$

Now, we can multiply the two numbers. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{18}{5}\times \frac{7}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify this product by swapping the denominators:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{18}{5}\times \frac{7}{3} & =\frac{18}{3}\times \frac{7}{5} \\  & =6\times \frac{7}{5} \\  & =\frac{42}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number:

$$
\frac{42}{5}=8\,\text{R}2=8\,\frac{2}{5}
$$
